synthetic_sources.content:
# Synthetic policy

## Purpose and scope
This fictional policy describes how an imaginary team prepares internal status reports. It applies to reports created by the Cedar, Birch, and Maple groups for internal planning. It does not apply to public announcements, personal notes, or customer communications. The policy is an invented test document and has no real organization or operational authority.

## Preparation
Each report should identify its reporting period, include a short summary, and cite the section supporting each factual conclusion. Contributors should distinguish a measured result from a forecast, keep units beside numeric values, and preserve relevant qualifications. When several source notes describe the same event, the report should combine them without counting the event twice. A report owner checks that all required sections are present before marking the report ready.

## Review and retention
A reviewer checks that dates and names agree across the included notes. Unresolved disagreements should be stated plainly rather than silently reconciled. Drafts may be revised during the current planning cycle. Once a report is accepted, the final copy is retained with its source references; obsolete drafts are not represented as current guidance.

## Exception
Archived reports are excluded from this policy's preparation and review requirements. This is the only exception stated in the fictional policy. Requests about archived material may still cite the archive record, but that citation does not make the archived report subject to the current-report workflow.

## Additional context
The report format is intended to make decisions traceable, not to prescribe a particular software package or writing style. The team may use tables when they clarify comparisons and may use prose when it better preserves context. None of those preferences changes the scope or the archived-report exception above. This synthetic passage is deliberately longer than a one-line lookup so the fixed task card can exercise document retrieval and summary workflows.
